C-TERMINOLOGY-RUSSIAN-NAMES.Summary: Use universal term headings and add researched Russian-language names to the Russian shared terminology reference.

Goals.Goal: Provide an established or context-qualified Russian-language name for all 71 entries, immediately after their universal term.
Preserve each edition's own definitions and project the additional names accurately into the Russian portal and search.

Constraints.Constraint: Authority: the user explicitly requested the additional Russian column, research of actual professional usage, a universal term heading, and the corrected label «Русскоязычный термин». This supersedes only the identical table-layout requirement in C-TERMINOLOGY-LANGUAGE-EDITIONS; earlier approved bundles remain unchanged.
Keep formal institutional wording, international naming rules, equivalent meanings, the four subject groups and operational definitions. Neither language has precedence.
Preserve unrelated workspace changes. Keep research rationale outside normative clauses; cite applicable sources without reproducing the conversation.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Corpus-wide terminology replacement, operational changes, apply/archive, commit, push or deployment.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: All four term tables use Universal term in English and Универсальный термин in Russian; only Russian has the following Русскоязычный термин column.
Every one of the 71 rows has a researched name or a clearly scoped corpus designation; protected brands retain their names.
Definitions, applications and table identities remain aligned; structural validation rejects unrelated or malformed additional columns.
Both universal and Russian-language names find the appropriate portal section; source checks, tests and generated-site checks pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Per-entry naming evidence and browser checks of four-column rendering and search in both languages.
